title: Stylometry's limits and unrun base rates in the authorship investigation
description: Standing claims from the authorship investigation set limits on what stylometry can show: genre separates more strongly than authorship, separability is not identity (Chatterton as Rowley separates from Chatterton as himself), and no measured property recovers master-student succession from heteronymic construction. Unbuilt tests list the base rates and runs still owed, among them residual-vs-total parity, comparanda for terminal aporia, the Pessoa leave-one-out folds, work-level and register-conditioned runs on Aristotle and Theophrastus. Frozen predictions order speaker tightness by constraint severity and distinguish engineered from natural ambiguity, beside readings of the Statesman's open genus and Plato's coin figure.

claims.statement:
**The corrected account.** Plato coins a name for a genus whose criterion is **issuing from oneself rather than relaying another's mind.** He notes the genus contains multiple sub-genera. He follows exactly one — the branch to kingship — because that is what the present inquiry is for. **He leaves the others unentered and unnamed.** Separately, he dismisses the relaying arts and concedes them the right to name themselves.

**The class is open by construction and marked as open.** The position that speaks from itself is named, is explicitly larger than any of its instances, and is abandoned mid-division with its remaining genera unentered.
